newsitem.title: USA: Clinton leads Dole by 10 points in Reuters poll.
newsitem.headline: Clinton leads Dole by 10 points in Reuters poll.

text.p: President Clinton surged to a 10-point lead over Republican Bob Dole and boosted Democratic chances in congressional races, the Reuter daily tracking poll said on Saturday.

The poll, conducted by John Zogby Group International, showed Clinton with 44.5 percent, Dole 34.3 percent and independent Ross Perot, 8.3 percent. Results were based on a three-day rolling average of surveys of more than 900 likely voters. The margin of error was 3.3 percentage points.

"Clinton's movement into a double-digit lead is putting Demcrats into the lead in the congressional 'generic' question," said pollster John Zogby. "This is the biggest lead for Democrats on that question that we've seen."
Republicans captured control of both houses of Congress in 1994 for the first time in 40 years.
When respondents were asked which party's candidate they would support in their local congressional district, 38.6 percent said the Democrat and 35.1 percent said the Republican.
The lead has switched hands since daily surveys began Sept. 28. Usually, the margin between the two parties was less than two points.
However, respondents were evenly divided when asked which party should control the House of Representatives or Senate.
Clinton has widened his lead over Dole since Oct. 8 but showed the greatest growth in the past couple of days. Zogby said Perot nearly doubled his support in the same period.
